challenges.headline: One invoice per contract assumed
challenges.premise: A signed contract produces a single invoice for the full amount.
challenges.alternative: A contract can require several invoices over time — milestone billing, recurring/subscription cycles, or partial payments — meaning the trigger should feed a billing schedule rather than a single document.
challenges.consequence: Building for a single invoice now means a costly rebuild the first time a milestone or recurring contract needs to be billed, since the data model and trigger logic would need to change, not just a rule.
challenges.recommendation: Confirm with the client whether any contract types require multiple or scheduled invoices before scoping the build.

challenges.headline: Immediate issuance on signature
challenges.premise: The invoice is created and effectively final the moment the contract is signed.
challenges.alternative: Creating the invoice as a draft pending finance review absorbs the risk of incomplete contract data at signature time and avoids consuming a legal invoice number on a document that might need correction.
challenges.consequence: Auto-issuing final invoices under French numbering rules is not easily reversible — an error discovered after the fact requires a credit note, not a simple fix, and burns a legal sequence number in the process.
challenges.recommendation: Validate with Finance whether auto-created invoices should land as draft-for-review or be issued outright.

challenges.headline: Signature as a clean, single trigger
challenges.premise: The contract-signed event fires once and reliably, so 'automatic' can mean synchronous, one-shot creation.
challenges.alternative: Treating the trigger as asynchronous and idempotent — with a visible pending state and safe handling of replays or late/out-of-order events — protects against duplicate invoices when the same signature event is redelivered, or when an amendment re-opens signature on the same contract.
challenges.consequence: A naive synchronous, non-idempotent trigger risks duplicate invoices reaching clients, which is a financial and compliance problem, not just a bug.
challenges.recommendation: Have engineering define the trigger's delivery guarantees and duplicate-detection rule before estimating the work.

Contract amendments re-triggering the signature event and firing unintended re-invoicing.
Permission or visibility changes to the shared invoicing module rippling into manually created invoices as well.

challenges.headline: One invoice per signed contract

challenges.alternative: Model invoicing as a billing schedule driven by the contract (single, milestone, recurring or partial) rather than a single creation event, since a contract is one-to-many with its invoices in this domain.
challenges.consequence: Building for a single invoice now means retrofitting a one-to-many billing model later the moment a milestone or recurring contract shows up — a much larger rework than getting the shape right first.
challenges.recommendation: Confirm with Finance whether billing is always single-shot or must support milestones/recurring terms before estimating.

challenges.headline: Auto-issue without review
challenges.premise: The request implies the invoice appears ready to send the instant the contract is signed.
challenges.alternative: Create the invoice as an editable draft awaiting finance validation, since amount, VAT and payment terms depend on contract data that may be incomplete exactly at the signature moment.
challenges.consequence: Issuing directly off a signature event risks generating a legally-numbered invoice with wrong or incomplete data, which under French numbering rules can't simply be edited afterward.
challenges.recommendation: Default the auto-created invoice to draft status pending finance sign-off, and confirm this with Finance before build.

challenges.headline: Signature fires exactly once
challenges.premise: The trigger is assumed to fire cleanly, once, per contract.
challenges.alternative: Treat the signed event as potentially repeatable (system retry, re-signature after correction, amendment re-triggering signature) and design invoice creation to be idempotent against a stable contract+state key.
challenges.consequence: Without idempotency, retries or re-signing after an amendment silently produce duplicate, legally-numbered invoices that are costly to void or correct.
challenges.recommendation: Define the idempotency key and retry-handling behavior before implementing the listener.

challenges.headline: One invoice per contract assumption
challenges.premise: The request treats 'invoice the contract' as producing exactly one invoice at signature.
challenges.alternative: Model invoicing as one-to-many from the start — a billing schedule sourced from the contract (milestones, recurring, partial) that can spawn zero, one, or several invoices — rather than a single document tied to a single event.
challenges.consequence: Building for a single invoice now means the whole feature gets rebuilt, not patched, the moment a milestone or recurring contract shows up.
challenges.recommendation: Confirm with Finance whether any current or near-term contracts require multiple invoices before locking the data model.

challenges.headline: Signature as the invoicing trigger
challenges.premise: Invoice creation is assumed to fire at the moment of contract signature.
challenges.alternative: Trigger on the contract start date or a defined billing schedule instead — decoupling the legal act of signing from the commercial act of billing.
challenges.consequence: Signature-triggered invoicing generates documents for deals that can still fall through, get amended, or shift terms before they actually start, forcing cancellations and credit notes.
challenges.recommendation: Validate the exact invoicing trigger point with Finance before wiring the event.

challenges.headline: Sync creation undecided
challenges.premise: The flow implicitly assumes invoice generation happens inline as part of signing.
challenges.alternative: Create the invoice asynchronously with a visible pending state, so missing billing data or a generation failure doesn't block or roll back the signature itself.
challenges.consequence: A synchronous design ties invoice-generation errors directly to the signature UX and risks failing the signature step for unrelated billing-data problems.
challenges.recommendation: Decide sync vs async explicitly, and design idempotent retries before implementation.
